items.title: Manuel "Fess" Manetta Interview, 1957-03-21
items.q: Well, during that time, he was playing for Spanish folk every night with Piron.

ctx.x: I know. But they weren't if you played sax out there, too, with him once.

Well, during that time, he was playing for Spanish folk every night with Piron. And he worked at his blueprint place on Camp Street. So what I loved, he was the first man bought a saxophone in the Orleans. Lou Warnick.

items.title: Manuel "Fess" Manetta and Edward "Kid" Ory Interview, 1958-08-26
items.q: AJ P. Ron, take the number, went to New York and had it published as Sister Kate.

ctx.x: That's the time I'd left him on top of the street, go. So crowded, you know. I had to get back home.

So when I came back to town, Joe had went to Chicago. Well, in 1917, Lewis was just playing three numbers. That's right. He played in the audience, he was a blues. He made a number called Wine and Grind. He named them. Sister Kate. Well, Sister Kate, take your finger out of Kattie's head. And then, of course, Joe Oliver and Jane Crying Swim, AJ P. Ron, take the number, went to New York and had it published as Sister Kate.
No, my mama's baby boy. Huh? I and my mama's baby boy. I've never seen the music. I've been trying to find it, but I can't find it in a place.
